label: Humanitarian and international response
description: NGOs, UN agencies, cluster partners and development programs responding to crises outside a single national emergency system: sudden-onset disasters, refugee influxes, outbreaks in camps, staff security incidents and supply pipeline breaks. Four variants: an international NGO country office, a coordination office with clusters, a response site and a headquarters crisis management team. All organizations, people and crises are fictional.

vocabulary.facility: the country office and the response sites (offices, warehouses, health posts and camps)
vocabulary.public: affected people, displaced families and host communities
vocabulary.frontline: programme officers, site and camp managers, logisticians, health and water and sanitation staff, drivers and community mobilisers
vocabulary.operationsCenter: the emergency coordination room or the headquarters crisis management room

it: shared drives, cluster mailing lists and meeting notes
3W (who does what where) matrix and dashboard
humanitarian data exchange platform and report library
beneficiary registration and case management database
fleet tracking and mobile data collection
shared services: email, directory and file sharing
ot: satellite phones and VHF/HF radio networks
generators and solar power at field bases
water treatment and chlorination at water points
cold chain for vaccines and medicines

roles.name: NGO Country Director
roles.description: Owns programme, staff and funding decisions in country, relations with the host government, and the call to hibernate, relocate or evacuate on the security manager's advice.

roles.name: Emergency Response Manager
roles.description: Sets the scope and sites of the response, chooses partners, reports to the cluster and decides which coordination gaps the organization will fill.

roles.name: Head of Logistics and Supply Chain
roles.description: Owns the pipeline, procurement, transport and warehousing; sees a stock break coming and decides whether to reroute, borrow or ask for a customs waiver.

roles.name: Security Manager
roles.description: Runs the security risk assessment, approves or refuses movements, records incident reports, shares alerts with other agencies and advises on hibernation or evacuation.

roles.name: Communications and Advocacy Lead
roles.description: Writes public statements and donor and partner messages, keeps them consistent with the headquarters line and the facts in the situation report.

roles.name: Grants and Donor Relations Manager
roles.description: Tracks funding against the response plan, tells donors about pipeline changes and incidents, and drafts appeal and reporting inputs.

roles.name: Humanitarian Coordinator
roles.description: Leads the in-country response through the cluster lead agencies, chairs the Humanitarian Country Team and recommends scale-up and an appeal.

roles.name: Coordination Office Head
roles.description: Convenes the Humanitarian Country Team, issues flash updates and situation reports and manages the shared information products.

roles.name: Cluster Coordinator
roles.description: Runs sector meetings, keeps the gap list, assigns gaps to partners and escalates to the Humanitarian Country Team what the cluster cannot close.

roles.name: Information Management Officer
roles.description: Builds the 3W (who does what where) table and map from partner reports, sets data sharing rules and publishes dashboards.

roles.name: Camp Manager
roles.description: Runs site services, registration, site planning and the community feedback channel for a displacement site or settlement.

roles.name: Site Health Coordinator
roles.description: Runs camp health surveillance, reports cases and deaths, and asks the sectors for water, sanitation and treatment capacity when an outbreak starts.

roles.name: Water, Sanitation and Hygiene Officer
roles.description: Keeps water supply, latrines and hygiene items in line with the population and the outbreak, and reports coverage by site.

roles.name: Protection Officer
roles.description: Monitors protection risks, referrals and access for people at risk, and raises incidents with the protection cluster.

roles.name: Crisis Management Team Lead
roles.description: Activates the crisis management team for a staff incident, keeps the decision log and owns the line to the country office, the family, legal counsel and the donor.

roles.name: Family Liaison Officer
roles.description: Is the one contact for a staff member's family, passes on only what the crisis management team has cleared and records each contact.

roles.name: Legal and Insurance Adviser
roles.description: Advises the crisis management team on legal duties, insurance and what may be said about a staff member in custody.

roles.name: Headquarters Media Lead
roles.description: Holds the media line, issues the holding statement and answers press and social media questions about a staff incident.

outsideParties: the host government's disaster management authority, its customs service and its health ministry
other NGOs and the national and local civil society organizations
UN agencies and cluster lead agencies
the refugee agency and the camp coordination partners
the military and police for civil-military coordination
shipping agents, port operators, banks and the telecom provider
the press, local broadcasters and social media
mediaChannels: a diaspora group on a messaging app
a community leader's radio call-in programme
a viral post about a distribution

sceneAnchors.public: a crowded distribution point outside a warehouse: families queuing in dust and sun, volunteers in bright vests, stacked sacks, a handwritten list board, daylight
sceneAnchors.control: an emergency coordination room in a rented house: laptops on folding tables, a wall map with pins, a whiteboard of gaps, a satellite phone on charge, fans running
sceneAnchors.exterior: a camp at the edge of a dry river plain: rows of white tents, water tanks on stands, a dirt road with a white four-wheel-drive vehicle, hills in haze

addedThreatFamilies.label: Sudden-onset disaster abroad
addedThreatFamilies.description: An earthquake, cyclone or flood in another country: the first 72 hours of assessment, cluster coordination, a 3W picture and an appeal.

phaseArc.title: Alert and first reports
phaseArc.goal: Early reports arrive before anyone knows the scale; organizations decide whether to deploy.
beats: A flash update with an unconfirmed casualty range
A national disaster authority statement that has not yet asked for international help
Partners ask who is leading coordination

phaseArc.title: First 24 hours
phaseArc.goal: Assessment teams deploy, the government request is clarified and cluster activation is requested.
beats: An assessment team cannot reach the worst-affected area
The Humanitarian Coordinator requests cluster activation
A customs delay holds relief items at the airport

phaseArc.title: First 72 hours
phaseArc.goal: A 3W picture builds up from partner reports and the gap list shows where nobody is working.
beats: Three partners report the same district while a neighbouring district has none
A cluster meeting produces a gap list with owners missing
An appeal needs a figure before the assessment is complete

phaseArc.title: First weeks
phaseArc.goal: Access constraints, funding and duplicated effort test the response plan.
beats: A bridge washout cuts a corridor
A donor asks why coverage in the north is low
Staff fatigue and rotation planning

phaseArc.title: Transition
phaseArc.goal: The response hands over to recovery planning and the team records what to change.
beats: A hot wash disagreement about when the gap list should have gone to the Humanitarian Country Team
A funding gap for the next quarter

decisionPointExamples: fill a coverage gap now with the organization's own stock, or wait for the cluster to assign it and risk a longer delay
escalate an unassigned gap to the Humanitarian Country Team now or give the cluster another day
launch an appeal on the first assessment figure or wait for a better one
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: a partner's 3W entry, an assessment figure for one district, a cluster gap list line, a flash update paragraph, an access note from a logistics cluster meeting
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: roads are cut, partners report late or in different formats, the assessment is incomplete, relief items are held at customs
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: the Humanitarian Country Team, the cluster coordinators, the host government's disaster authority and the donors
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Use a fictional country, province and crisis. Cluster activation is requested by the Humanitarian Coordinator and decided by the Emergency Relief Coordinator with the endorsement of the IASC Principals, unless the scenario states the 2025 Humanitarian Reset arrangement in which the Humanitarian Country Team decides which clusters to activate. Keep numbers in the 3W table, the gap list and the flash update consistent with each other.

decisionMustMention.description: a coordination decision (cluster, gap, appeal or escalation to the Humanitarian Country Team)

addedThreatFamilies.label: Refugee influx
addedThreatFamilies.description: People cross a border faster than a site can register and shelter them; the refugee coordination model applies, not cluster activation.

phaseArc.title: Arrival
phaseArc.goal: Numbers at the border rise and the first reception capacity is full.
beats: A border post reports a rate far above the plan
A transit centre runs out of water containers
Local authorities ask who is in charge

phaseArc.title: Registration and reception
phaseArc.goal: Registration throughput lags arrivals and a queue grows.
beats: Registration kits break down
Unaccompanied children are identified in the queue
A partner proposes a site on a floodplain

phaseArc.title: Site and services
phaseArc.goal: A site is chosen and the sectors scale services to the population.
beats: Latrine coverage falls below the site plan
The camp manager asks for a coordination meeting no one chairs
A community leader raises a complaint about food

phaseArc.title: Consolidation
phaseArc.goal: Roles settle between the refugee agency, the government and partners, and the plan is costed.
beats: A donor asks for a costed plan by Friday
The government changes the site boundary

decisionPointExamples: accept a site that is quick to open but at risk of flooding, or hold arrivals at the border longer
prioritise registration of families or of unaccompanied children first when capacity is short
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: an arrivals tally from a border post, a registration throughput figure, a site plan note, a community complaint
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: registration equipment fails, arrivals exceed the plan, a site is not ready, interpreters are missing
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: the refugee agency, the host government, camp management partners and the sector leads
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Refugee settings use the refugee coordination model led by the refugee agency with the government; do not activate clusters in this family. Treat people as actors with agency. Keep registration and arrival numbers consistent.

decisionMustMention.description: a site, registration or capacity decision with the refugee agency or the government

addedThreatFamilies.label: Outbreak in a displacement site
addedThreatFamilies.description: Cholera or measles appears in a camp: surveillance, treatment capacity, water and sanitation, and communication with the community.

phaseArc.title: First cases
phaseArc.goal: A cluster of cases is noticed and reported through the site health post.
beats: Three deaths from watery diarrhoea in one block
The health post asks for a case definition
A rumour that the water is poisoned

phaseArc.title: Confirm and declare
phaseArc.goal: The team confirms the disease and decides whether to declare an outbreak response.
beats: A rapid test result and a laboratory delay
Pressure to avoid the word cholera
The health cluster asks for a daily surveillance report

phaseArc.title: Response
phaseArc.goal: Sectors scale treatment, water, sanitation and messaging together.
beats: Treatment centre beds run short
Chlorine stock is low at the water points
Community feedback shows people do not trust the new latrines

phaseArc.title: Control and close
phaseArc.goal: Cases fall, the team reviews the curve and the site returns to routine services.
beats: A secondary peak in a neighbouring block
The outbreak is declared over after a stated period

decisionPointExamples: declare an outbreak response on the clinical picture now, or wait for laboratory confirmation
move treatment beds from a quiet block to the busy one and accept a gap there
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: a surveillance line list, a daily case count, a water point chlorine reading, a community feedback entry
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: laboratory transport is delayed, chlorine and oral rehydration supplies run short, roads limit access, rumours spread
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: the health cluster, the water, sanitation and hygiene cluster, camp management and the site's community committees
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Keep clinical content at the level of surveillance, coordination and supplies: counts, attack rate, case fatality, treatment capacity. Give no treatment protocols beyond naming oral rehydration and referral. Use the epidemiology toolkit for curves when it is on.

decisionMustMention.description: an outbreak response decision (declaration, treatment capacity, water or the health cluster)

addedThreatFamilies.label: Staff security incident
addedThreatFamilies.description: A staff member is detained, kidnapped or injured, or a convoy is attacked: the crisis management team's decisions, communications and family liaison. Decision and communications level only.

phaseArc.title: Incident report
phaseArc.goal: The country office reports a staff incident and the security manager records it.
beats: A movement report is overdue by two hours
A partner reports a checkpoint incident involving a vehicle with the organization's markings
The first report is incomplete and conflicts with a second

phaseArc.title: Team activation
phaseArc.goal: Headquarters activates the crisis management team and sets its roles and cadence.
beats: The crisis management team meets for the first time
Legal asks what may be said and to whom
The country office asks whether to stop all movements

phaseArc.title: Family liaison and information control
phaseArc.goal: One voice speaks to the family, the media, the donor and other agencies.
beats: A relative calls the country office directly
A social media post names the staff member
Another agency asks for the alert

phaseArc.title: Resolution decisions
phaseArc.goal: The team decides on movements, hibernation or relocation and what to share with other agencies.
beats: Hibernate a field base or keep a programme running
Share a security alert with other agencies at the level of the information-sharing framework

phaseArc.title: Recovery and review
phaseArc.goal: The staff member's return, care and a review of the decision log.
beats: Staff care and debrief arrangements
A review of decision timing against the first report

decisionPointExamples: stop all movements in the area now, or let essential programme travel continue under a stricter approval
hibernate a field base or relocate staff
share a security alert with other agencies now, or wait for more detail
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: an overdue movement report, a partner's call, a social media post, a family contact, a security alert from another agency
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: communications are down, the first report is incomplete, the family contacts the wrong person, the media runs ahead of the facts
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: the crisis management team, the family liaison officer, legal counsel, other agencies' security focal points and the donor
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Stay at the level of decisions, communications and coordination. Do not write negotiation tactics, ransom amounts or mechanics, techniques for evading or resisting detention, or tactical security procedures. Participation in an inter-agency security collaboration framework does not make the UN responsible for an NGO's security. Include a content notice for facilitators.

decisionMustMention.description: a staff safety decision (movement, hibernation, relocation, family contact or alert sharing)

addedThreatFamilies.label: Supply pipeline break
addedThreatFamilies.description: A port closure, customs hold or access constraint makes stock run out before the next shipment arrives.

phaseArc.title: Early signal
phaseArc.goal: Consumption runs ahead of the forecast and a shipment slips.
beats: A warehouse report shows fewer days of stock than planned
A shipment's arrival date moves by a week

phaseArc.title: Break forecast
phaseArc.goal: The pipeline dashboard shows a break date inside the lead time of any reorder.
beats: The forecast break falls before the next shipment can arrive
A customs hold notice arrives for a container

phaseArc.title: Options
phaseArc.goal: The team weighs rerouting, borrowing stock, rationing and a waiver request.
beats: A reroute costs more and adds days
A partner offers to lend stock at a price
A waiver request needs a government signature

phaseArc.title: Recovery
phaseArc.goal: Stock arrives, rations are restored and donors are told what changed.
beats: A ration cut was announced too late
The donor asks for a revised delivery schedule

decisionPointExamples: cut rations now to stretch stock, or hold the full ration and risk a harder cut later
reroute a shipment by a longer, costlier route, or wait for a customs waiver
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: a warehouse stock figure, a shipment status line, a customs hold notice, a consumption report from distribution
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: customs and port delays, truck availability, a washed-out road, bank or payment delays
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: customs, the logistics cluster, the shipping agent, the donor and distribution partners
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Keep stock, consumption, lead times and the break date consistent: days of stock equal stock on hand divided by daily consumption. Use fictional commodities and quantities.

decisionMustMention.description: a pipeline decision (ration, reroute, waiver, borrowing or telling the donor)

addedThreatFamilies.label: Funding gap
addedThreatFamilies.description: Funding falls short of the response plan and programmes must be cut or prioritised.

phaseArc.title: Signal
phaseArc.goal: Funding status shows the appeal well below the plan.
beats: The funding status page shows a low share funded
A donor delays a tranche

phaseArc.title: Prioritise
phaseArc.goal: Clusters and organizations decide what to cut or protect.
beats: A cluster is asked to reduce its target by a quarter
A partner threatens to leave a site

phaseArc.title: Communicate
phaseArc.goal: Messages to donors, partners and communities must agree.
beats: A community meeting asks why food rations shrank
A donor asks for a prioritised list

phaseArc.title: Adjust
phaseArc.goal: The plan is revised and the gap is tracked.
beats: A revised appeal is issued
A partner's exit leaves a coverage gap

decisionPointExamples: protect life-saving programmes and cut the rest, or spread cuts evenly across sectors
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: a funding status figure, a donor email, a cluster prioritisation note, a community feedback entry
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: donor processes are slow, figures differ between sources, partners give conflicting numbers
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: donors, the cluster coordinators and the Humanitarian Country Team
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Keep funding figures consistent between the funding status, the appeal and every message. Use fictional donors and amounts.

addedThreatFamilies.label: Beneficiary data breach
addedThreatFamilies.description: A registration or distribution list is exposed: staff must protect the people on it, notify those who must be told and keep programmes running.

phaseArc.title: Discovery
phaseArc.goal: A list of fictional beneficiaries is found exposed.
beats: A staff member finds a shared folder open to anyone
A partner reports a stolen laptop with registration data

phaseArc.title: Contain and assess
phaseArc.goal: The team decides what was exposed and who is at risk.
beats: The list includes a protection caseload
Legal asks about reporting duties

phaseArc.title: Notify and protect
phaseArc.goal: Affected people, partners and donors are told what they need to know.
beats: A community meeting asks if their names are public
A donor asks for a written report

phaseArc.title: Review
phaseArc.goal: Data sharing rules and storage are changed.
beats: The cluster information management officer asks for a data sharing review

decisionPointExamples: tell affected communities now with partial facts, or wait until the scope is known
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: a file access log, a partner call, a registration list extract with fictional names, a complaint from a community member
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: the scope is unclear, the offline copies cannot be traced, the partner is slow to respond
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: the data protection focal point, legal counsel, the protection cluster and the donor
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Use fictional people and lists. Do not include real names or identifiers. Keep the response at the level of containment, notification and protection decisions.

addedThreatFamilies.label: Communications loss in the field
addedThreatFamilies.description: Phones, radio, satellite links or the network fail, and the team must coordinate and keep staff safe without its usual tools.

phaseArc.title: Degradation
phaseArc.goal: Links drop or slow in the field offices and the sites.
beats: Radio checks are missed at three bases
The satellite link is congested

phaseArc.title: Fallbacks
phaseArc.goal: Teams switch to radio, runners and paper forms.
beats: A 3W update arrives by paper days late
A movement approval cannot be sent

phaseArc.title: Safety
phaseArc.goal: Staff safety decisions must be made with less information.
beats: A convoy is out of contact
The security manager sets a check-in rule

phaseArc.title: Restoration
phaseArc.goal: Links return and the team reconciles what was missed.
beats: Backlogged reports arrive at once
A duplicate movement request is approved twice

decisionPointExamples: hold all movements until contact is restored, or let convoys proceed on a pre-agreed schedule
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: a missed radio check, a paper form, a delayed report, a bounced email
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: power, antenna, congested satellite links or a cut cable
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: the telecom provider, the security manager, other agencies and the headquarters crisis management team
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Describe what players see in their tools and what they decide; do not give network configuration or repair detail.

decisionMustMention.description: a fallback or movement decision during the loss

noiseExamples: a vendor offering generators the programme does not need
a cluster mailing list thread about meeting times
a visiting delegation asking for a tour
an old report re-sent by mistake
a request to join another working group
pressureExamples: a donor asking why coverage in one district is lower than in another
a government official demanding that a distribution be moved
a headquarters director asking for an answer to a media question in an hour
a community leader threatening to block a road over food rations
a family member demanding to know where a staff member is
agencyPattern: OCHA|UNHCR|WFP|UNICEF|WHO|IOM|IFRC|Red Cross|Red Crescent|Humanitarian Country Team|HCT|IASC|Humanitarian Coordinator
